title: Why Paul commands sharp rebuke and why all things are pure to the pure
english: Since Paul often teaches gentleness with praise, but found that the Cretans needed the goad of rebuke, as it were, he said for this reason: “Rebuke sharply” (Titus 1:13). “All things indeed are pure to the pure” (Titus 1:15). God made all things pure; but if they are impure, the accusation touches the one who made them.

orientation: Oecumenius is explaining Paul's instructions in Titus 1:13b and 1:15-16, first why Paul commands sharp rebuke despite often teaching gentleness, then why all things are pure to the pure.

title: Confessing God but denying him by deeds
english: And this is what it means to profess to know God while denying him by their deeds (Titus 1:16). Paul showed that women are called to an inheritance, for he would not have called them reverent (Titus 2:3).

title: Incorruptibility of mind and dignity of work
english: Paul understood incorruptibility as a quality of the mind, and dignity as a quality of one's work, so that a person would keep away not only from corrupt deeds but also from corrupt thoughts.
